title: Iterative shot-diff playbook: templates, probes, failure catalog
content:
Purpose
- Working notebook for exploring small-k variations and their effect on behavior across tasks. Goal: build a compact prompt library where each template has a documented shot-diff profile (what changes when you add/remove or replace shots). For PLG experiments and regression detection.

Quick definitions
- shot-diff: difference in model outputs when k-shot examples are changed or reordered. includes label flips, hallucinations, format drift.
- canonical template: base instruction + placeholders for examples + closing instruction.
- probe: a fixed set of evaluation queries used to surface brittle cases.

Notes and heuristics so far
- Diversity beats repetition: few-shot sets that are semantically diverse expose more stable behavior than many near-duplicate examples.
- Anchor example: a single strongly representative example often reduces hallucination but can bias style. track tradeoff.
- Order sensitivity: randomizing order across evaluation runs reveals order-dependent failure modes; use 5 random seeds.

Experiment log (selected)
1) 2024-11-07 3-shot support intent classification probe\- Template: short instruction, 3 examples, final user query expected label only\- Shots used: 1 canonical high-signal, 2 edge cases\- Observed: model returned correct label 86% with canonical anchor first, 64% when anchor absent. Reordering caused label confusion for 7 of 50 queries.\- Takeaway: prefer 1 anchor + 2 diverse negatives; include explicit label line 'Answer: <label>' to reduce freeform.

2) 2024-12-03 summarization microtemplate test (2 vs 4 shots)\- Template: instruction to summarize in 1 sentence; examples show abbreviations allowed\- 2-shot baseline introduced more verbosity and hallucinated entities in 12/100 cases; 4-shot with tighter formatting examples reduced hallucinations to 3/100 but increased tendency to copy phrasing.\- Note: add explicit "do not introduce new entities" line in instruction.

3) 2025-01-18 code-fix prompt ablation\- Task: given failing pytest snippet, propose minimal fix.\- 0-shot: too generic, suggests major refactor 40% of time.\- 1-shot anchored with small failing example: 0-shot->1-shot delta reduced extreme rewrites by 70%.

Prototype templates (copyable)
- classification compact template
  Instruction: Classify the user's last message into one of: question, request, bug-report, praise, other. Return only the label.
  Examples: (3)
    - User: I cant login, keeps saying invalid token
      Answer: bug-report
    - User: How do I change my API key?
      Answer: question
    - User: Love the new dashboard layout!
      Answer: praise
  Final: User: <INPUT>
  Expected: Answer: <label>

- summarization microtemplate
  Instruction: Produce a one-sentence summary, do not add facts not in the text. Use neutral tone.
  Examples: (2)
    - Text: Our Q3 revenue grew 12% over Q2, driven by enterprise sales.
      Summary: Revenue rose 12% in Q3, led by enterprise deals.
    - Text: The server crashed after the migration and was restarted by ops.
      Summary: Migration caused a server crash that ops restarted.
  Final: Text: <INPUT>
  Expected: Summary: <one sentence>

Failure catalog (short form)
- label ambiguity: model invents a new label when example labels are not exhaustive. mitigation: add an explicit 'otherwise: other' example.
- instruction bleed: model follows example wording too closely, copies phrasing. mitigation: paraphrase examples.
- format drift: outputs in sentence form instead of single token. mitigation: use explicit 'Return only:' line and show formatted examples.
- hallucination under low-shot: introduces entities not in input for summarization and QA. mitigation: stronger negative examples, explicit refusal sentence.

Ideas to add to library
- shot-diff fingerprint: a small vector/descriptor summarizing how outputs change when each shot is toggled; store as plain text tags for now (eg 'sensitive-to-order', 'anchor-stabilizes', 'hallucinates-on-entities').
- canonical probe suite per task: 100 handcrafted queries with golden labels and known brittle cases.
- automated shot selection: greedy pick maximizing diversity across simple embedding space.

Open questions / TODO
- how to codify order-sensitivity threshold for alerting regressions in CI? (suggest: >10% label flip across 5 random orders triggers)
- when does adding a shot reduce calibration vs increase bias? need a small param sweep across k=0..5 on 3 tasks.
- export format for library entries: JSONL per template with fields [id, instruction, shots, probe-set-id, tags, shot-diff-notes]. (note: this is external artifact idea; keep drive doc agnostic)

Next steps (short)
- finalize canonical prompts for classification and summarization by 2025-02-28
- run 5-order seeds for current probes and record shot-diff fingerprints (Arjun to run)
- add 100-probe suite skeleton to prompt-repo (Lena to draft)

Quick links / references
- internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-repo/pull/412
- JIRA: JIRA-ML-1289 (prompt library infra)

Notes to self
- keep examples terse; long examples increase token cost without consistent benefit\- record exact seed and order used for each run in metadata when adding to repo

end of scratchpad
